title: Degree-zero direct-image comparison is compatible with coefficient restriction
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, $\varphi:A\to B$ a homomorphism of finite commutative rings, $F$ a sheaf of $A_X$-modules and $G$ a sheaf of $B_X$-modules on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $u:F\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi G$ be an $A_X$-linear morphism. Use the K-injective derived direct images $Rf_*^A,Rf_*^B$ and the canonical restriction-of-scalars comparison $c: Rf_*^A\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi Rf_*^B$ of [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars]. Under the degree-zero augmentation isomorphisms $f_*F\cong\mathcal H^0(Rf_*^A(F[0]))$ and $f_*G\cong\mathcal H^0(Rf_*^B(G[0]))$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero], the morphism
$$\mathcal H^0\bigl(c_{G[0]}\circ Rf_*^A(u[0])\bigr):\mathcal H^0(Rf_*^A(F[0]))\longrightarrow\mathcal H^0(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi Rf_*^B(G[0]))$$
is the underived map $f_*u:f_*F\to f_*\operatorname{Res}_\varphi G=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi f_*G$ [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image]. Here restriction of scalars is exact, so commutes with $\mathcal H^0$, and the augmentation identifications are those obtained from nonnegative injective resolutions. Thus the comparison retains the actual section map, not merely its source and target objects.

proof.text: Use the small skeleton and coefficient universe of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Applied to each constant commutative ring sheaf, [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] gives Grothendieck module categories and K-injective resolutions for all complexes. They have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] therefore supplies ordinary injective resolutions $s:F[0]\to L$, $a:G[0]\to J$, and $b:(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi G)[0]\to I$, all zero in negative degrees. By [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], $L,J,I$ are K-injective. Write $r,s_Y$ for restriction of scalars on $X,Y$, respectively, to distinguish it from the augmentation $s$. By [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars], these functors are exact and $r(a)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 013K (lemma-injective-resolutions-exist), 070J (lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective), and Injectives 079H/079P; applied on the chosen small ringed sites

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], the derived morphisms $Qb\,(Qr(a))^{-1}:QrJ\to QI$ and $Qb\,Q(u[0])\,(Qs)^{-1}:QL\to QI$ lift to chain maps $v:rJ\to I$ and $h:L\to I$. The same bijection into the K-injective target $I$ shows $v\,r(a)$ is homotopic to $b$ and $hs$ is homotopic to $b\,u[0]$. Each pair consists of maps from a complex concentrated in degree zero to $I$. Its possible homotopy has its only relevant component in $I^{-1}=0$, so the degree-zero maps are actually equal; the other degrees of these source complexes vanish. Thus $v\,r(a)=b$ and $hs=b\,u[0]$ as chain maps. Since $b$ and $r(a)$ are quasi-isomorphisms, $v$ is a quasi-isomorphism (apply cohomology and cancel the isomorphism induced by $r(a)$). Consequently $v:rJ\to I$ is a K-injective resolution, although $rJ$ need not be K-injective.

source.place: Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective), morphisms into a K-injective target; the subsequent homotopy equation is written explicitly

proof.text: The functors $f_*^A,f_*^B$ are additive and left exact by [lem-weil-proetale-module-direct-image-left-exact]. Apply part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] to the three nonnegative resolutions. Denote the resulting isomorphisms by $\alpha_F:f_*F\to\mathcal H^0(f_*^A L)$, $\alpha_G:f_*G\to\mathcal H^0(f_*^B J)$ and $\alpha_r:f_*rG\to\mathcal H^0(f_*^A I)$. Each is induced by applying $f_*$ to the corresponding augmentation. Direct image and coefficient restriction commute on objects and maps by the formula $(f_*M)(V)=M(V\times_YX)$ in [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image]: restriction changes only the scalar action, and both actions send a local coefficient through the same constant-ring homomorphism. Hence $f_*^A r=s_Yf_*^B$ on complexes. Exactness of $s_Y$ in [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars] identifies $\mathcal H^0(f_*^A rJ)$ with $s_Y\mathcal H^0(f_*^B J)$; its augmentation is $s_Y\alpha_G$, abbreviated $\alpha'_G$.

Compute derived morphisms using [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation] with resolutions $s,b$. Its map formula says $Rf_*^A(u[0])$ is represented by $Q(f_*^A h)$. To compute $c$ at $G[0]$, apply [lem-sf-normalized-derived-comparison-common-resolution] with its source functors $F=f_*^A$, $G=f_*^B$, its exact functors $r,s_Y$, and its successive resolutions $a:G[0]\to J$, $v:rJ\to I$. Existence of resolutions was established in Step 1 and the equality $f_*^A r=s_Yf_*^B$ in Step 3. Its normalization hypothesis is exactly the inverse-on-resolutions normalization in [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars]. Since its composite resolution is $v\,r(a)=b$, the conclusion says that, under the canonical resolution identifications, $c_{G[0]}$ is $Q(f_*^A v)^{-1}:Q(f_*^A I)\to Q(f_*^A rJ)$. In particular this inverse exists. Thus the composite in the item is represented by $Q(f_*^A v)^{-1}Q(f_*^A h)$. This calculation uses no claim that restriction of scalars preserves K-injectivity.

proof.text:
Put $V=\mathcal H^0(f_*^A v)$ and $H=\mathcal H^0(f_*^A h)$. The strict chain-map equalities in Step 2 give
$$V\alpha'_G=\alpha_r,\qquad H\alpha_F=\alpha_r\,f_*u.$$
Indeed compose each proposed equality with the inclusion of degree-zero cycles into the degree-zero term. The resulting equations are respectively $f_*v^0\,f_*r(a)^0=f_*b^0$ and $f_*h^0\,f_*s^0=f_*b^0\,f_*u$, exactly the degree-zero components of those chain-map equalities. All relevant complexes have zero degree-minus-one term, so their degree-zero cohomology is their kernel of $d^0$ and that inclusion is monic. This proves both equations without an additional naturality assertion. By Step 4, $V$ is invertible. Therefore
$$\mathcal H^0(c_{G[0]}\circ Rf_*^A(u[0]))\,\alpha_F=V^{-1}H\alpha_F=V^{-1}\alpha_r f_*u=\alpha'_G f_*u.$$
Both augmentation maps are isomorphisms by Step 3, so this is precisely the asserted equality with the underived $f_*u$ under the prescribed identifications.
